chapters.1.meaning: Bathsheba and Nathan act before Adonijah can secure the throne. David publicly names Solomon as the next king.
chapters.1.lds: Who speaks for Solomon when David must choose the next king?
chapters.2.meaning: Solomon secures his rule by removing rivals. His orders include deaths and the loss of Abiathar’s priestly office.
chapters.2.lds: How does Solomon explain his orders against each rival?
chapters.4.meaning: Solomon’s court needs food from across the kingdom. Local officers supply the king and his household.
chapters.4.lds: Who provides the food that supports Solomon’s court?
chapters.5.meaning: Hiram supplies wood and skilled help. Solomon also forces men to work on the building project.
chapters.5.lds: What does temple building require from the workers and their families?
chapters.9.meaning: God’s promise calls for continued faithfulness. Solomon’s buildings and trade also depend on workers and foreign help.
chapters.10.meaning: The queen tests Solomon’s wisdom with questions. His answers and wealth impress her.
chapters.10.lds: What impresses the queen besides Solomon’s wealth?
chapters.13.meaning: An older prophet lies about God’s command. The visiting prophet trusts him and dies on his way home.
chapters.13.lds: Why does the visiting prophet accept a claim that changes his earlier command?
chapters.14.lds: How does Ahijah’s message affect Jeroboam’s wife and child?
chapters.15.meaning: The kings make different choices about worship. Their wars also shape life in both kingdoms.
chapters.15.lds: What does Asa give away to gain help against Baasha?
chapters.16.meaning: Plots and battles bring rapid changes of kings. Ahab’s marriage to Jezebel leads into Elijah’s story.
chapters.16.lds: How do the changes of kings affect their families and towns?
chapters.17.meaning: The widow shares food despite her fear of hunger. Her later grief leads her to question Elijah.
chapters.18.meaning: The people must choose whom to worship. Fire answers Elijah’s prayer. The victory also ends in killing Baal’s prophets.
chapters.20.lds: Why does the prophet challenge Ahab after his victory?
chapters.21.lds: How does Ahab gain from Jezebel’s plot against Naboth?
people.queen-sheba.meaning: She questions Solomon herself and praises his wisdom. She brings gifts from her own kingdom.
people.ahijah-shiloh.meaning: Ahijah first promises Jeroboam a kingdom. He later announces judgment on Jeroboam’s family.
people.adoram.meaning: Rehoboam sends Adoram to the northern tribes. They stone him during their break from the king.
people.bethel-old-prophet.meaning: He lies to bring the visiting prophet home. He later mourns the man his lie helped destroy.
people.asa.meaning: Asa removes objects used to worship other gods. He pays Syria to attack Baasha.
people.jehu-hanani.meaning: Jehu warns that Baasha’s family will fall because of its harmful rule.
people.zimri.meaning: Zimri kills Elah but rules for only seven days. He burns the palace around himself.
people.omri.meaning: Omri builds Samaria as a new capital. The book also condemns his worship practices.
people.tibni.meaning: Some Israelites choose Tibni while others follow Omri. Omri gains full rule after Tibni dies.
people.hiel.meaning: Hiel rebuilds Jericho and loses two sons. The chapter links these losses with Joshua’s earlier warning.
people.obadiah-palace.meaning: Obadiah hides and feeds prophets whom Jezebel wants to kill.
people.elijah-servant.meaning: Elijah sends him to look toward the sea. His cloud report signals the coming rain.
people.hazael.meaning: God tells Elijah to appoint Hazael as Syria’s king. His later rise appears in 2 Kings.
people.jehu-nimshi.meaning: God names Jehu as a future king. Second Kings tells how he takes power.
people.ahab-prophets.meaning: They promise Ahab victory in battle. Micaiah’s warning challenges their agreement.
people.zadok.meaning: Zadok anoints Solomon. Solomon later places him in Abiathar’s priestly office.
people.bathsheba.meaning: Bathsheba urges David to keep his promise to Solomon. She later carries Adonijah’s request.
people.david.meaning: David orders Solomon’s crowning and gives him final advice. He dies after arranging the change of king.
places.jerusalem.summary: Solomon rules from Jerusalem and builds the temple here.
places.gibeon.summary: Solomon offers sacrifices at Gibeon. God appears to him here in a dream.
places.tyre.summary: Hiram rules the coastal city of Tyre. Its wood and workers help Solomon build.
places.gezer.summary: Pharaoh takes Gezer and gives it to his daughter, Solomon’s wife.
places.edom.summary: Solomon’s sea trade passes through ports in Edom. Hadad later challenges his rule there.
places.jericho.summary: Hiel rebuilds Jericho during Ahab’s reign. The notice recalls Joshua’s warning.
places.en-rogel.summary: Adonijah holds a feast at En Rogel to gather support for his kingship.
places.gilead.summary: Gilead lies east of the Jordan. Elijah comes from this region.
places.dan.summary: Jeroboam places one golden calf at Dan to draw worship away from Jerusalem.
places.sidon.summary: Sidon is linked with Jezebel’s royal family and worship of other gods.
